inventedEvidence.evidence: 'Because this fault keeps happening even after you've checked the catches' - the customer had only just looked at the catches and had not said it tripped again afterwards

blockingLoop.evidence: After the customer answered 'its about 5 years old. i use it most days', the assistant replied almost verbatim: 'I need to know how old this appliance is and roughly how many times you use it each week.'

rationale: The assistant got the safety handling right from the first turn: stop using, stop resetting, unplug, engineer/electrician, and it correctly named door interlock switches as a likely cause with only a safe unplugged visual check. However it never asked the key discriminating questions (does the RCD hold with it unplugged, extension lead, other socket), slightly overstated the evidence ('keeps happening even after you've checked the catches'), and framed the 'click or bang' as arcing caused by door debris with more confidence than warranted. The final turn repeats the previous message nearly word for word and re-asks the age and usage questions the customer had just answered, so the conversation stalled without ever advising that a 5-year-old budget Russell Hobbs is probably a replace-not-repair case.
